headline: No dip to buy: BTC flat at $84.1k as ETF flows turn 2026 green, Iran talks collapse
summary: As of 18:20 UTC on Saturday 26 September there is no live dip in any of the three: BTC is $84,061.60 against an $84,090.50 open (-0.03%) inside an $83,619.60-$84,314.70 range, ETH $2,687.05 (-0.16%) in a $22 range, and SOL $121.31 (-0.66%) after a flush to $119.84 was bought straight back, leaving weekly changes of +3.3% BTC, +1.7% ETH and +9.1% SOL. The news underneath is worse than the tape: Trump confirmed today he rejects Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, Iran's military answered that all US deployment centres in the region will be targeted if Washington attacks, Saudi air defences shot down Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh and a missile at Khamis Mushait, and UKMTO says Hormuz commercial traffic is still about 75% below pre-conflict levels with US pump prices at $4.49 a gallon. Against that, the money flow is the strongest in a year - US spot bitcoin ETFs took about $2.98bn over seven straight inflow days to 26 September, $2.4bn in the 21-25 September week alone (IBIT $1.2bn, FBTC $701.7m), which flipped 2026 to roughly +$887m after being $5.8bn negative on 13 July - and Friday's record $15.9bn BTC plus $2.1bn ETH options expiry cleared without incident. Positioning is not crowded: Hyperliquid funding is a uniform 0.00125%/h on all three, BTC and SOL futures trade at a discount to spot (-0.048% and -0.005%), open interest is $3.14bn / $2.96bn / $682m, and only 64 items came through in 24 hours. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite 62.8, both Greed, so the mood is confident but the danger is a Sunday-night gap from the Middle East or a 10-year yield that is already at a 19-year high, not an existing washout.

BTC.note: $84,061.60, dead flat on the session in an $83,619.60-$84,314.70 range on $3.14bn of open interest with funding at 0.00125%/h and futures 0.048% below spot - no dip trigger, and for context the history file records 92.9% of 28 stored BTC dips recovering +1.5% within 14 days (median 5.0 h, 78.6% inside 24 h) and 100% of the 7 that occurred during greed.

ETH.note: $2,687.05, off 0.16% inside a $2,676.84-$2,698.71 range and still the laggard at +1.7% on the week, on $2.96bn of open interest and a futures premium of just 0.011%; the SEC's 25 September staff FAQs on staking receipt tokens are a fundamental positive that has not moved price.

SOL.note: $121.31, down 0.66% from a $122.12 open and the only one with real range - the drop to $119.84 was bought back to mid-range - and at +9.1% it is by far the strongest of the three on the week, with $682m of open interest and a flat 0.00125%/h funding rate pointing to give-back after a rally rather than distribution.

drivers.title: Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz roadmap; Iran's military threatens all US bases in the region
drivers.detail: Trump told reporters on 26 September that he rejects Iran's proposal - submitted via Qatar by foreign minister Abbas Araghchi to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within seven days in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, unfreezing assets and easing oil sanctions - saying Iran 'outsmarted themselves' and wants a deal because 'they have no money coming in', and posting a map labelling the waterway the 'Trump Strait'. Iran's military replied through Mehr that all US deployment centres and interests in the Middle East will be targeted if Washington attacks; Saudi-led air defences intercepted Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh and a ballistic missile at Khamis Mushait this morning, UKMTO puts Hormuz commercial traffic about 75% below pre-conflict levels, and the Wall Street Journal reports Trump expects US bombing to resume after the November midterms.

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETFs turn 2026 positive: seven straight inflow days, $2.4bn week
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs have taken in about $2.98bn over seven consecutive sessions from 17 to 26 September, including $134.5m on Friday and roughly $999m on Monday 21 September, the biggest single day since 6 October 2025. The 21-25 September week totalled $2.4bn, the largest since October 2025, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $1.2bn and Fidelity's FBTC at $701.7m; that turns 2026 flows positive at about +$887m after a $5.8bn deficit on 13 July, with cumulative inflows near $58.0bn and net assets $108.42bn. Decrypt puts the average ETF holder's cost basis at $81,722, so the typical fund buyer went back into profit on 21 September for the first time since January - real bid underneath a deteriorating news tape.

drivers.title: 10-year at 5.17%, a 19-year high, with another Fed hike 63-70% priced for October
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.17% after a three-session sell-off took it to about 5.20%, the highest since 2007, following the Fed's first rate increase in three years last week; CME pricing and prediction markets put a further 25bp hike at the 27-28 October FOMC at 63-70%. Thirty-year mortgage rates climbed above 7% for a fifth straight week and CoinDesk noted on 25 September that bond volatility surged while bitcoin and Wall Street stayed calm. That divergence is the main macro risk here: crypto is not pricing the rates move, so the adjustment, if it comes, arrives as a gap rather than a grind.

drivers.title: Record $18bn options expiry cleared Friday 25 September and took the pinning flow with it
drivers.detail: About $15.9bn of bitcoin options and $2.1bn of ether options expired on Deribit at 08:00 UTC on Friday 25 September, the largest settlement of 2026 and roughly 37% of Deribit's outstanding BTC open interest, with max pain at $76,000, heaviest calls at $85,000, $90,000 and $100,000, and a 0.70 put/call ratio. Price went through it without breaking - Decrypt described the rally slowing rather than reversing - but dealer hedging around those strikes had been holding the $83,000-$85,000 range together, and with the book gone the next few sessions have less mechanical support in either direction.

drivers.title: SEC staff say staking receipt tokens are not securities; Peirce leaves on 2 October
drivers.detail: SEC staff published FAQs on 25 September stating that staking, including liquid staking where the provider issues a tradable receipt token, generally falls outside the Howey test, provided the token does not alter the rights attached to the staked coins, does not set or add rewards and the provider does not lend, pledge or reuse the deposits. It is staff guidance rather than law, and it lands as Commissioner Hester Peirce - the commission's steadiest crypto advocate - confirmed 2 October as her last day, shortly after the Senate cloture vote on the CLARITY Act failed and the Blockchain Association lost its leadership. The direction of travel for ETH staking products is friendlier; the people and the statute behind it are less settled.

drivers.title: Bitget's $387m breach is still leaking: hacker moved $83m of XRP that cannot be frozen
drivers.detail: Bitget now puts the 24 September breach at about $387-388m across a limited number of hot wallets, and on 26 September the attacker moved roughly $83m of stolen XRP that Ripple has no ability to freeze; Circle and Tether froze only small amounts, 218,023 USDT and 99,990 USDC, before the rest moved. Withdrawals restart in stages from Monday 28 September at 08:00 UTC, Bitcoin first, and CEO Gracy Chen has said the patterns resemble groups previously linked to North Korea without confirming attribution. The exchange says its protection fund covers the loss, so this is a confidence risk rather than a solvency one - but it is the live crypto-specific event most capable of producing a panic candle this week.

watch.what: Oil and index futures reopen. This is the first price to see Trump's rejection of the Hormuz roadmap and Iran's threat against US bases, after WTI had already fallen about 7.4% last week on the assumption a deal was coming. A gap up in crude pushes the 10-year off 5.17% and is the most plausible route to a genuine crypto dip inside 48 hours.

Bitget restarts withdrawals in stages, Bitcoin first, then ETH, USDT and the rest through 2 October. A queue that clears quietly removes the last acute crypto-specific risk; a second delay or another revision to the $387m figure is the clearest candidate for a flush.

US personal income and outlays with the PCE deflator, forecast +0.4% m/m headline and +0.3% core, both accelerating from 0.2%, plus ADP at about +70k and JOLTS openings near 7.23m. With an October hike 63-70% priced and the 10-year at a 19-year high, a firm PCE is the most direct scheduled pressure on crypto's range.
ISM manufacturing PMI and China's September PMIs - the warm-up to payrolls, and the read on whether last week's unusually strong US composite PMI was a one-off.

September employment report, consensus about +100k nonfarm payrolls from +162k with unemployment rising to 4.2%. A hot print into a Fed already priced to hike again is the cleanest macro path to a dip; the same day is Hester Peirce's last at the SEC.

Iranian retaliation risk after the rejection. Houthi launches at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait were intercepted this morning and Iran's military has now publicly threatened US regional bases; watch for tanker incidents, a US strike, or new Treasury sanctions on Iranian crypto networks, all of which have moved BTC before.
FOMC decision at the end of the 27-28 October meeting, roughly 63-70% priced for a further 25bp hike after last week's first increase in three years.
